question: What twist did Thomas Hobbes add to the old puzzle of a ship repaired plank by plank?
answer: A second ship. Suppose someone keeps each old plank as it comes out, then reassembles them in the same order. Two ships now claim to be the original: the repaired one that never stopped sailing, and the rebuilt one of the first wood. Two ships numerically the same, Hobbes wrote in 1655, is absurd.
move: When two things claim one identity, ask what the name was tracking.
ask: When two things both claim to be 'the same one', what was the name tracking?
reference: Hobbes, De Corpore II.11.7, in Calkins (ed.), The Metaphysical System of Hobbes, Open Court, 1905
